code:
{% raw %}
name: Publish Docker Image

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'   # triggers on: git tag v0.1.0 && git push --tags

jobs:
  push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to ghcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract version tag
        id: meta
        run: echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
            ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
{% endraw %}
description: A GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on version tags, logs in to ghcr.io, and builds and pushes the image with both a latest tag and the version tag.

steps.description: This is `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`. The page says to create it so GitHub Actions builds and pushes the image automatically whenever you push a version tag. The raw markers are template lines around the workflow. `name` labels the workflow, and `on.push.tags` triggers it on tags that start with `v`, such as `v0.1.0`.
The workflow has one job, `push`, running on `ubuntu-latest`. It requests two permissions: read access to the repository contents and write access to packages.
The first two steps check out the repository and log in to ghcr.io. The login uses `github.actor` as the username and `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` as the password.
The third step writes the git tag name into an output named `tag`, using `GITHUB_REF_NAME`.

The last step builds and pushes the image with `docker/build-push-action@v5`. It uses the current directory as context, pushes the image, and tags it twice: once as `latest` and once with the version tag from the previous step.
